title: Wire up your first schematic
summary: Place a couple of symbols, connect them with a wire, name the net, and run the electrical rules checker — the core loop of drawing a schematic in KiCad's Schematic Editor.

steps.note_guide: Start by placing a component. This opens the symbol chooser — pick a part (say a resistor) and click to drop it on the sheet. A symbol is the schematic representation of a real part.
steps.note_expert: Place a symbol from the library chooser.

steps.note_guide: Add a power symbol (like GND or +5V). Power symbols tell KiCad which nets are power rails, and nets with the same power symbol are automatically joined.
steps.note_expert: Place a power port for your rails.

steps.note_guide: Draw a wire between two pins to connect them. Click the first pin, then the second. Wires are the electrical connections of the schematic.
Give the net a name with a net label. Two wires with the same label are the same net even without a drawn connection — handy for keeping the sheet tidy.
steps.note_expert: Label the net; same label = same net.

steps.note_guide: Where two wires cross and should connect, drop a junction. Without it, crossing wires are NOT connected — a classic source of silent schematic bugs.
Finally, run the Electrical Rules Checker. It flags unconnected pins, conflicting outputs, and missing power — catch these now, before they reach the PCB.
steps.note_expert: Run ERC; resolve violations before layout.
